summary: Shell research program phase 6 after a dive wave: one opus agent harvests the new consolidations, appends the landing report to the topic map, applies the stop condition, and commissions the next wave (revised staged briefs plus follow-ups) or declares ready-to-draft with binding authoring notes
logs: Verdict: ready-to-draft · next wave 0 · IDs 389 · MUST 263 · families 21 · contradictions 25

harvest.verdict_reason: Research has nothing left that blocks drafting. The held-out round produced 15 failure classes (9 MUST, 6 SHOULD); each has a planted violation and a compliant twin, except the PowerShell half of SH-CI-33 and the grep half of SH-CORE-16. All 15 now carry final IDs marked provisional: true. Every amended cell was fitted on the same 64 trees, so those trees are spent. The clean round the wave plan requires therefore becomes a confirmation round against the drafted artifacts on fresh trees (orchestrator decision). Every open question is classified as a dated re-check, a measurement the corpus cannot supply, an owner decision with its default applied, or work for the confirmation round. 23 new cross-consolidation contradictions (X59-X83) are resolved, each naming the ID that keeps the text. The binding authoring notes, including the dialect, drop list, budgets and per-unit sources, are appended.
frame_corrections: The research stop condition is met at the drafts: the clean round runs as a confirmation round on the drafted artifacts over fresh trees. The 64 held-out trees are spent, because every amended cell was fitted on them.

The funnel's ~60-100 shipped rules applies per language surface. This set covers seven surfaces plus emitters and installers, so budgets apply per depth file, and selection drops pointer rows and catalog-only rows, not measured MUST rules.
A bash RETURN trap persists: it re-fires after a later source and under set -T, never on later plain calls (heldout conflict 1).

On Windows PowerShell 5.1 the BOM is the fix and ASCII-only is not the hazard (47 of 82 non-ASCII files carry a BOM and work). ASCII-only stays required for irm|iex-delivered files, #! files and emitted PowerShell.
Shebang detection on the exact text #!/bin/sh is wrong: '#! /bin/sh', '#!  /bin/sh' and CRLF shebangs are real shapes.

The program's harnesses are not inherently read-only: a third-party --install honoured an inherited ZDOTDIR and wrote to the real ~/.zshrc. Harnesses that run third-party installers must use env -i (SH-CORE-16).
plant/trailing.sh is withdrawn as SH-INST-01 evidence (heldout conflict 4).
$PSVersionTable.OS is free text and cannot identify a platform.
On Windows, elvish reads %XDG_CONFIG_HOME%\elvish\rc.elv or the RoamingAppData known folder, never ~/.config. nu's $nu.data-dir is %AppData%\nushell, moved by XDG_DATA_HOME and not by %APPDATA%.
ble.sh discards a PROMPT_COMMAND write only in the window from ble-attach to the first prompt, and only on v0.4.0-devel3 and the nightly. Wave 3's 'after attach' overclaimed.
The Artifact set glob list lacks **/.gitlab-ci.yml and **/.gitlab-ci/*.yml. Both need --allow-absent; neither is live in www-setup.
'Not in scope: cmd.exe batch' means authored .cmd/.bat files. Emitted Batch (SH-EMIT-48..50) is in scope.

SH-SEC-09 binds every POSIX shell. SH-SEC-13 covers git credentials (GIT_ASKPASS with a 0600 file, credential.helper store, the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT triple, git 2.31+). SH-SEC-14 covers cargo tokens (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, CARGO_REGISTRIES_NAME_TOKEN, cargo login on stdin). files() uses 'shfmt -f --'. The vendor exclusion is ':(exclude,glob)**/vendor/**'. The merged s05 cell is in the topic-map notes section 5(c).

SH-CI-11 and SH-CI-12 are NOT dropped: they ship as self-contained copies.

Verification dialect for every shipped cell (SH-GATE-21..31). Shape: git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- 'PATHSPEC' | xargs -0 -r grep -H -n -e 'PAT' --. Shell content via files()/shfiles(). Quoted pathspecs (':(glob)**/NAME', ':(exclude,glob)**/DIR/**'); never an unquoted glob or **. grep options only -E -F -e -H -n -l -L -c -o -q -s -v -w -x -i --. One -e per top-level alternative; \| under -E is a literal pipe. -- before operands for grep, shfmt and shellcheck. Always xargs -0 -r. Explicit operands, never implicit stdin or cwd. No $(...) or backticks. No angle-bracket placeholders; use a quoted variable. The SH-GATE-25 PREFLIGHT line opens each block, extended with the block's own tools. Pass = empty stdout and empty stderr; never read an inline cell's exit status; never 2>/dev/null. Waiver filter: grep -v -e 'TOKEN: *[^ ]'. No command inside a table cell; escape | as \| in cells. Lookaround, multi-line, CR or byte-class matches go to an awk checks/NAME.sh (POSIX awk, LC_ALL=C). Shipped scripts use the exit map 0/1/69/74/78/79 (PS wrappers 0/1/2). Python extractors run as python3 -I, and a non-zero status is a failure. Every translated cell is re-watched red/green in the confirmation round.

Portability. Supported executors: GNU, busybox 1.37 with git, uutils 0.10+, Git Bash 5.2.15. macOS and BSD are 'unverified: read only' on every cell. Cells use only the BSD-documented grep options, xargs -0/-r, tr, POSIX awk and git; never sed -i, readlink -f, stat -c, date -d, find -printf or grep -P. checks/*.sh start #!/bin/sh and pass dash 0.5.12, busybox ash 1.37 and bash 3.2 --posix. PS assets state the engines they ran on (5.1.26100.9444, 7.4.7, 7.6.6).

Budgets. Indexes under 200 lines, MUST rows first. Depth files need a TOC over 100 lines and no chains; a cross-family ID appears only as attribution '(also X)'. One row per ID (ID, imperative, one-line rationale, verification, severity, Scope line), grouped by check. Program-set line caps: dialect 230, userland 190, errors 330, expansion 230, security 260, gates 340, testing 230, ci 340, zsh 180, fish 190, nushell 170, elvish 100, emit 460, installers 220, PS compat 150, PS errors 130, native 70, encoding 160, PS gates 240, PS security 180. SKILL.md body at most 500 by check-artifacts.py, target 460. About 374 shipped rows plus 3 PS-CORE rows; every MUST names its script kind.

Version dating. Every version-specific claim names tool and version and is dated 2026-10-11. Never 'latest'. Items with a known end carry 'until DATE' (pwsh 7.4 2026-11-10, ubuntu-latest 2026-11-19, fish 3.6.0 floor 2028-06-30). macOS/BSD claims are tagged 'unverified: read only'. Provisional rows carry provisional: true. Pinned decisions are marked 'pinned decision (adopter may override)'.

Pinned decisions and defaults; do not re-litigate. Exit maps (installer 0-7, gate 0/1/69/74/78/79, Swift carve-out frozen to 16 sites). Error model by kind (SH-ERR-23). Floors: bash 3.2.57; sh POSIX.1-2017 plus probes; zsh 5.8 authored / 5.0.8 emitted; fish 3.6.0-4.9.3; nu-range header; elvish 0.18.0-0.21.0; PowerShell 5.1 for iex and installers, 7.6 for repo scripts. Four .shellcheckrc keys, no SC2312. actionlint at default severity. zizmor regular at medium. bats 1.14.0. Pester 6.2.0 exact (5.9.1 for Pester 5). ShellCheck 0.11.0, shfmt 3.13.0+, PSSA 1.25.0. Skip budget zero. Four waiver tokens with a reason. The program files nothing. Owner defaults: PS-ENC-01 BOM-aware, SH-INST-23 root-by-design exception, SH-TEST-25 exclude list, M-X-05 left as residue.

Skills scope. shell-integration, installer-script, shell-port and shell-diagnose carry procedures only. A duplicated MUST appears in a '| # | Finding | Rule |' table citing MUST IDs only, never rule-ID-first and never a SHOULD. Commands live in fenced sh blocks, not table cells. Each skill ends with a ranked 'What agents get wrong' table. shell-integration ships corpus.txt and the harnesses in references/. installer-script marks SH-INST-22/23 and PS-SEC-14 provisional.

Confirmation round, after drafting, on fresh trees only (never the 64 held-out trees, the 41 corpus repos or the fleet). It replays every heldout-amended cell unmodified, every translated cell, the merged s05/s02 cells, the gate script with -- on its 33 plants, the 15 provisional checks, the PowerShell half of SH-CI-33 and a non-validating busybox:1.37 SH-INST-07 run. All harnesses run under env -i (SH-CORE-16). A clean round clears provisional: true; a new class reopens only its family.
